name: Brown Butter Tahini Cabbage with Sumac & Mint
description: Charred cabbage wedges served on sourdough toast with a nutty brown butter tahini sauce

equipment.item: Large high-sided sauté pan or skillet
equipment.notes: For searing cabbage, must be oven-safe OR transfer to baking dish
Large enough for a whole cabbage

ingredients.notes: Keep core intact so wedges hold together

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: get out 1 small bowl for the sumac-zest mixture, 1 small bowl or container for lemon juice, 1 small dish for garnish items, and a measuring cup. Clear your cutting board area for the cabbage.
prep_steps.notes: Having everything ready prevents scrambling when the brown butter is at the critical moment

prep_steps.instruction: Cut cabbage into 8 wedges through the core, keeping core intact so wedges hold together
prep_steps.notes: The core is essential - it holds the leaves together during searing and roasting

prep_steps.instruction: Season both sides of all cabbage wedges generously with kosher salt
Zest half of the lemon into the first small bowl
prep_steps.notes: Only need zest from half the lemon

prep_steps.instruction: Juice the entire lemon into a separate small bowl or container
prep_steps.notes: Will use half during cooking, half at the end

prep_steps.instruction: Measure 1/2 teaspoon sumac into the bowl with lemon zest. Measure additional sumac into the garnish dish.
prep_steps.notes: The garnish dish will hold sumac and mint for finishing

prep_steps.instruction: Pick mint leaves from stems, add to the garnish dish with reserved sumac
Measure tahini into the measuring cup. Have ready near stove.
prep_steps.notes: Stir tahini well in jar before measuring - oil separates

cook_steps.instruction: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) with rack in center position
Heat olive oil in large high-sided sauté pan over medium heat

cues.visual: Oil shimmers and flows easily when pan is tilted

cook_steps.instruction: Sear cabbage wedges in batches until nicely browned on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side

cues.visual: Deep golden-brown char marks, edges beginning to caramelize
cues.audio: Active sizzle when cabbage hits pan

cook_steps.warnings: Don't overcrowd pan - work in batches of 2-3 wedges

cook_steps.instruction: Nestle all seared cabbage wedges together in pan, drizzle with white wine vinegar

cues.aroma: Sharp vinegar smell that quickly mellows

cook_steps.instruction: Transfer pan to oven and roast for 30 minutes

cues.visual: Cabbage is tender when pierced with a knife, edges deeply caramelized

cook_steps.instruction: When cabbage has 15 minutes left, start the sauce: melt butter in a large sauté pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until milk solids turn golden then deep brown (4-5 minutes)

cues.visual: Butter foams, then foam subsides. Milk solids on bottom go from white → golden → amber brown
cues.audio: Crackling subsides as water cooks off

cook_steps.warnings: Watch carefully - brown butter can burn quickly. Reduce heat if browning too fast.

cook_steps.instruction: Reduce heat to low. Add sumac-zest mixture to brown butter and stir

cues.visual: Sumac blooms and disperses into the butter
cues.aroma: Lemony, tangy note joins the nuttiness

cook_steps.instruction: Add tahini to the pan and swirl to combine into a smooth sauce. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm over low heat.

cues.visual: Sauce is smooth, creamy, and pourable

cook_steps.warnings: Don't let sauce boil or it may separate
Time this so bread is warm when cabbage comes out

cook_steps.instruction: Remove cabbage from oven. Squeeze half the lemon juice over the wedges

cues.audio: Sizzle as juice hits hot cabbage

cook_steps.instruction: Pour the warm sauce directly over the cabbage wedges, covering them as much as possible. Squeeze remaining lemon juice over top.

cues.visual: Sauce pools around and coats the wedges

finishing.instructions: Place one cabbage wedge on each slice of toasted sourdough. Drizzle with any remaining sauce from the pan. Sprinkle with reserved sumac and scatter mint leaves over top. Serve immediately while warm.
finishing.make_ahead: Cabbage can be seared ahead and refrigerated. Bring to room temperature before roasting. Make sauce fresh.
finishing.storage: Best served immediately. Leftovers can be refrigerated for 2 days but will lose crispness.

notes: The brown butter is the star - don't rush it. You want deep amber, not just golden.
Salted butter is specified and recommended - it adds flavor to the sauce.
The core of the cabbage is essential - it holds the wedges together.
If your pan isn't oven-safe, transfer seared cabbage to a baking dish before roasting.
